title: Murdoku
desc: A murder on the floor plan: place everyone so that every statement is true, and find out who did it. Every case has exactly one solution.

clue.bare: Was standing on bare floor, no furniture.
clue.inner: Was away from every outer wall.
clue.company: Was not alone in the room.

accuse.title: Who did it?
accuse.text: Everyone is in the right place. Who was in the same room as {victim}?
accuse.closed_text: Only {killer} was with {victim} in the room «{room}».

status.placing: {placed} of {total} placed. Tap a square for {name}.
status.marking: Mark is on: tap squares to cross them out.
status.broken: Everyone is placed, but the story does not add up. At least one statement is still false.
status.pick_first: Pick a person first, then a square.
status.blocked_table: Nobody can stand on a table.
status.blocked_plant: Nobody can stand on a plant.
status.blocked_shelf: Nobody can stand on a bookshelf.
status.locked: {name} was placed by a hint and stays put.
status.accuse: Every statement holds. Now name who did it.
status.alibi: {name} has an alibi. Look at who shares a room with {victim}.
status.revealed: Here is the solution. «Next case» takes you on.

guide.title: How to play
guide.goal: There has been a murder in a house. You put everyone in their place on the floor plan and so find out who was alone with the victim.
guide.rule_rows: Every row and every column holds exactly one person.
guide.rule_furniture: Nobody can stand on a table, plant or bookshelf – those squares are hatched. Chairs, rugs and beds are fine.
guide.rule_clues: Every statement is true. «Right beside» means sharing an edge, not a corner. North is up, west is left.
guide.rule_killer: Exactly one other person is in the victim's room. That person is guilty.
guide.place: Pick a person below the floor plan or in their statements, then tap a square. Tap a placed person to pick them up again.
guide.mark: «Mark» crosses out squares where nobody can be. On a computer, right-click does the same.
guide.hint: «Hint» puts one person in their correct place. A case solved with hints counts as solved, but not for your best time.
guide.finish: Once everyone is right, you name the guilty person. «Next case» starts the next one straight away.

tips.title: Solving tips
tips.start: Start with the most precise statements. «Was in the room …», «Was sitting on a chair» or «Was in row 2» often leave only one or two squares.
tips.blocked: Hatched squares drop out at once. Nobody ever stands there.
tips.lines: Once a person is fixed, their row and column are taken for everyone else. Cross them out with «Mark».
tips.last: If a row or column has only one free square left, someone must stand there. Ask yourself who fits.
tips.alone: «Was alone in the room» keeps everyone else out of that room. «Was not alone» needs a second person in the same room.
tips.victim: The victim's room holds exactly two people. Anyone who is surely elsewhere is cleared.
tips.compare: «Further north than …» works both ways: one person is not in the bottom row, the other not in the top row.
tips.negative: «Was not in the room …» helps too: if it holds for almost everyone, only one person is left for that room.
tips.assume: If you are stuck, try an assumption. If it leads to a contradiction, the opposite is true.
